# ALS evidence packet — draft v1

This curated input is not a comprehensive review. Every method receives the same UTF-8 file. Summaries are original paraphrases. Bibliographic metadata and abstracts were checked through the public NCBI ID converter and PubMed EFetch on 2026-10-05. Selected studies predate 2025; this does not remove knowledge already in a model's training. Co-Scientist outputs are not included.

## Research question

Propose one specific, testable hypothesis connecting phosphorylation of a nuclear-pore-complex nucleoporin to ALS-related neuronal dysfunction. Explain the causal chain, distinguish an initiating mechanism from a downstream response, and propose an experimental strategy that discriminates the hypothesis from an alternative. Identify supported premises, speculative bridges, and a falsifying observation. This adapts Co-Scientist Supplementary Note 10; nucleoporin phosphorylation is not supplied as an established ALS cause.

## S1 — TDP-43 and nuclear-pore dysfunction

Chou et al. (2018), *TDP-43 pathology disrupts nuclear pore complexes and nucleocytoplasmic transport in ALS/FTD*. Nature Neuroscience. DOI: `10.1038/s41593-017-0047-3`; PMID: `29311743`; PMCID: `PMC5800968`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29311743/).

Nuclear-pore and transport components were associated with insoluble TDP-43 aggregates. Disease-linked TDP-43 disrupted nucleoporin localization and nuclear transport in experimental cell systems; relevant pore pathology was observed in ALS tissue. This supports examining the connection between TDP-43 pathology and transport disruption. It does not identify a nucleoporin phosphorylation event as the initiating cause or establish the same sequence in every ALS subtype.

## S2 — C9orf72-associated transport defects

Zhang et al. (2015), *The C9orf72 repeat expansion disrupts nucleocytoplasmic transport*. Nature. DOI: `10.1038/nature14973`; PMID: `26308891`; PMCID: `PMC4800742`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26308891/).

Expanded C9orf72 repeat RNA was linked to altered RanGAP localization and impaired nuclear import in models and patient-derived neurons. Manipulations of transport or repeat-RNA-associated mechanisms modified model phenotypes. This supplies a genetic-context-specific route to transport dysfunction. It does not show that sporadic ALS arises by the same route or directly establish a nucleoporin phosphorylation mechanism.

## S3 — A stress-granule-independent route

Gasset-Rosa et al. (2019), *Cytoplasmic TDP-43 De-mixing Independent of Stress Granules Drives Inhibition of Nuclear Import, Loss of Nuclear TDP-43, and Cell Death*. Neuron. DOI: `10.1016/j.neuron.2019.02.038`; PMID: `30853299`; PMCID: `PMC6548321`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30853299/).

Persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies could form independently of conventional stress granules. They recruited or mislocalized transport-associated proteins and were associated with impaired transport, nuclear TDP-43 depletion, and cell death. Phosphorylated TDP-43 accumulated in these assemblies. That is not itself evidence of nucleoporin phosphorylation. The experimental perturbations do not establish that every physiological ALS trajectory begins in this way.

## S4 — A stress-granule-associated route

Zhang et al. (2018), *Stress Granule Assembly Disrupts Nucleocytoplasmic Transport*. Cell. DOI: `10.1016/j.cell.2018.03.025`; PMID: `29628143`; PMCID: `PMC6083872`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29628143/).

Cellular stress recruited transport factors into stress granules and impaired nucleocytoplasmic transport. Altering stress-granule assembly modified transport defects and disease-model phenotypes. This provides a sequestration-based alternative to an intrinsic pore-modification hypothesis. Read alongside S3, it does not justify assuming that conventional stress granules are required for every TDP-43-associated transport defect.

## Evidence boundaries

- These selected passages do not establish that nucleoporin phosphorylation initiates ALS. Label a proposed kinase, modification site, or interaction as an assumption unless a supplied source supports it.
- Specify the ALS context; do not assume a universal mechanism across genetic and sporadic disease.
- Distinguish pore alteration, transport-factor sequestration, and failure secondary to broader stress.
- Explain temporal and perturbational evidence that would distinguish cause from consequence.
- Propose a research hypothesis rather than claiming a mechanism or treatment has been validated.


Proposed answer (the answer to evaluate):
Hypothesis title: Nup98 phosphorylation after stress-granule-independent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assembly sustains nuclear-import failure in TDP-43 proteinopathy.

Hypothesis and context. In TDP-43 proteinopathy models relevant to sporadic ALS, Nup98 phosphorylation is a required pore-intrinsic intermediate only after a discovery gate selects it. Cytoplasmic TDP-43 de-mixing is the initiating event. Gated Nup98 phosphorylation is proposed to sustain import failure by changing NPC composition. Nuclear TDP-43 loss, wider transport failure, and neuronal death are downstream. The claim is limited to this TDP-43 context and stays provisional until NPC phosphoproteomics ranks Nup98.

Supported premises. Insoluble TDP-43 associates with nuclear-pore and transport components, and disease-linked TDP-43 disrupts nucleoporin localization and nuclear transport in cells, with pore pathology in ALS tissue [S1]. This is a TDP-43–pore link; a phosphorylation cause is unidentified. C9orf72 repeat RNA tracks with RanGAP mislocalization and impaired import, and transport manipulations modify that genetic context [S2]. Stress-granule-independent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies mislocalize transport proteins and accompany import failure, nuclear TDP-43 loss, and death, and they contain phosphorylated TDP-43 [S3]. Stress-granule recruitment of transport factors also impairs transport, and changing stress-granule assembly modifies that phenotype [S4]. [S3] versus [S4] separates the two routes. These sources leave nucleoporin phosphorylation unestablished.

Speculative bridges. Nup98, its sites, and the kinase are assumptions. Unverified prior knowledge: FG-nucleoporins can be phosphorylated in mitosis or stress outside ALS. Assemblies are assumed to direct that kinase to Nup98 so the mark alters NPC composition and sustains import failure. Composition, meaning Nup98 retention and a short nucleoporin-localization panel, is the only step under test.

Alternatives. Sequestration of transport factors in stress granules can block import without a covalent pore change [S4]. Direct nucleoporin mislocalization by TDP-43 can leave phosphorylation as a bystander [S1]. RanGAP mislocalization can explain C9orf72 import failure without Nup98 phosphorylation [S2]. Nonspecific stress can impair import as a downstream consequence.

Discriminating preclinical test. In iPSC-derived motor neurons or primary rodent neurons, induce a preregistered cytoplasm-enriched TDP-43 de-mixing construct that yields persistent assemblies without conventional stress granules [S3]. Suppress stress granules by one preregistered genetic reduction of a single named core scaffold, dosed to block stress-granule markers after a standard stress pulse. Arms: de-mixing plus suppressor (Arm 1), de-mixing with stress granules intact (Arm 2), suppressor alone (Arm 3), and C9orf72 repeat RNA without engineered TDP-43 assemblies (Arm 4) [S2]. Keep the suppressor only when Arm 3 NLS import and nuclear-to-cytoplasmic TDP-43 stay within a prespecified equivalence band of untreated cells; if import shifts, discard that suppressor and exclude its Arm 1 data.

Before any allele, time-resolved NPC-fraction mass spectrometry ranks FG-nucleoporin phosphopeptides against assembly onset, nuclear TDP-43 loss, and death. An Nup98 cluster is editable only when NPC-fraction recovery, stoichiometry above a prespecified Arm 1 baseline margin, and a rise after assemblies and before death markers all hold, and only when that cluster ranks first on this joint score. Absence of such a cluster, or failure to rank first, falsifies this Nup98 claim. Other nucleoporins stay descriptive context.

Replace only gated sites at near-endogenous dosage with phospho-null or phospho-mimetic Nup98 and hold total TDP-43 constant. Add kinase knockdown or inhibition, interpretable only if gated phosphosites fall while assembly burden stays inside the Arm 1 equivalence margin. Readouts are NLS-reporter import, nuclear-to-cytoplasmic TDP-43, NPC composition, RanGAP localization, stress-granule markers, and delayed death. Import rescue with composition unchanged relative to phosphorylated Nup98 retires the compositional bridge. Arm 1 is supported if the mark follows assemblies, precedes death, and phospho-null Nup98 or kinase blockade preserves import and Nup98 retention despite assemblies. Define R as fractional NLS-import rescue by phospho-null versus wild-type Nup98. Context specificity holds only if Arm 4 R is at most 0.25 times Arm 1 R, and fails if Arm 4 R is at least 0.50 times Arm 1 R. Ratios between those bounds are indeterminate.

Falsifying observation. Arm 1 import failure without an Nup98 site that is NPC-recovered, above the stoichiometry margin, and earlier than death markers falsifies the claim. Phospho-null Nup98 that lacks the gated mark, with unchanged timing and severity of import failure, nuclear TDP-43 loss, and death, also falsifies it. A mark appearing only alongside death markers is a late correlate. Joint loss of the transport defect and of Nup98 phosphorylation after accepted suppression favors sequestration [S4]. Flat import across both phospho-alleles falsifies the sites. Clearing the mark by kinase blockade while assemblies persist and import stays failed falsifies the kinase step.

Limitations. Sites and the kinase are gate outputs. Parallel phosphorylation of other nucleoporins can false-negative Nup98, which the rank list records, while the claim stands or falls on Nup98. Phospho-mimetics miss timing and place. Cultured neurons compress years-long disease. C9orf72 and SOD1 transfer, and any therapy, remain untested.

Ranked proposal:
Nup98 phosphorylation after stress-granule-independent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assembly sustains nuclear-import failure in TDP-43 proteinopathy
